findings.message: This fixes AC-3 only where the reviewer pointed: the Features grid. Other claims on the same page still describe unbuilt modules as available. Hero.tsx:10 says "Payroll, leave and billing stay up to date through chat". The page DESCRIPTION at apps/web/app/(public)/welcome/page.tsx:20 says agents "keep HR, payroll and billing current through MCP". Open Graph and Twitter also use that DESCRIPTION. Payroll and billing are not shipped, and areas.ts now marks both as Coming, so the page contradicts itself. marketing-areas.test.ts only checks AREAS, so it cannot catch this. Fix: drop or reword the payroll and billing claims in the hero and the metadata description. Then extend the test to cover every marketing claim, for example by checking the hero and description text against the Coming set.
findings.scenario: A signed-out visitor opens / → the hero says payroll and billing are kept current through chat, while the feature grid below lists "Payroll for Sri Lanka and Australia" and "Contracts and billing" as Coming. A shared link's OG description makes the same false claim.

findings.message: knownOrigin() uses a bare catch {} that turns every error from baseUrl() into null. That includes loadEnv()'s "invalid environment configuration" error, for example a malformed AMAX_BASE_URL that fails z.url(). So "origin not configured" and "config could not be read" give the same result, and both are silent. The page then drops its canonical and OG URLs, robots drops its sitemap line, and sitemap.xml returns 200 with an empty list. AC-7 fails in production, and nothing logs or flags it. This is the case the previous finding raised ("nothing flags it"): the localhost URL is gone, but the silence is not. Fix: catch only the expected "AMAX_BASE_URL unset" case. Let invalid configuration throw, or at minimum surface it, for example by logging a fixed message once in production. Add variants to site-origin.test.ts: production with a malformed AMAX_BASE_URL, and production with it unset (does it flag?).
findings.scenario: NODE_ENV=production, AMAX_BASE_URL="amax.example" (no scheme), no DATABASE_URL → /welcome renders with no canonical or og:url, /sitemap.xml returns an empty urlset with 200, and nothing is logged.

findings.message: The test does not check the Coming set against modules/*/module.ts. It checks a hard-coded list of planned ids, and those ids are not linked to the Coming entries, which are free text. If a planned module ships, or a new unbuilt claim is added, the Coming chip can go stale and the test stays green. Add a module id to each Coming entry and assert that it is not installed. Then each live claim is checked against the installed modules and each Coming entry against the modules that are not installed.
findings.scenario: Ship modules/expenses → the grid still shows "Expenses" as Coming and the test still passes.
